research_attempts.query_text: Arthur M Thurston; NARA OSS index and public Archives context; CIA Reading Room or equivalent official-source check; exact-name and meaningful variants; OSS and military clues; employer and occupation 1940; obituary, institutional, newspaper, directory, Library of Congress and archival searches; Box 777; protected identifiers used privately only when defensible
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Unbridged namesakes, search snippets, unsourced genealogy, people-finder pages, modern records, postwar-only leads and sources without an OSS, protected-identifier or Box-file bridge were not assigned. Spelling variants were search aliases only. Differing protected identifiers and substantive name conflicts were rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: A signed 1943 FBI legal-attaché letter and an authoritative NARA-RG-226-based account of the July 1945 OSS/China leadership were inspected directly. The earlier government assignment is documented, but immediacy is not. Exact-name OSS, employer, occupation, obituary, institutional, newspaper, official-domain, CIA Reading Room-equivalent and Library of Congress searches were checked as applicable. The index page, Army technical documentation and occupation-code pages were inspected directly. No search-result snippet was used as sole final evidence, no access control was bypassed, and no authenticated NARA Catalog API call was made.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 777 for corroborating identifiers, the immediate pre-OSS affiliation and the last civilian employer before wartime service.
